ShortDef: A private folder of Python packages for one project, so projects do not clash.
Details: `python -m venv .venv` creates one; activating it points `python` and `pip` at it. Every project should have its own, and the dependency list should be committed.
WhenToUse: From the first line of any project that has dependencies.

ShortDef: Python's standard package installer; PyPI is the public index it downloads from.
Details: `pip install name` fetches a package and its dependencies. Pin versions in a requirements or lock file so builds are repeatable.

ShortDef: The single configuration file for a modern Python project: metadata, dependencies and tool settings.
Details: Replaces setup.py and scattered config files. Build tools, linters and formatters read their settings from it too.
WhenToUse: Starting or modernising a project or a library.

ShortDef: A very fast Python package and project manager written in Rust, replacing pip, venv and more.
Details: `uv add`, `uv run` and `uv sync` manage environments and a lock file in one tool, often an order of magnitude faster than pip.
WhenToUse: New projects, CI speed-ups, and anywhere pip feels slow.

ShortDef: Optional annotations that describe what types a function expects and returns.
Details: Python ignores them at runtime; editors and checkers (mypy, pyright) use them to find bugs and power autocomplete. Libraries like Pydantic and FastAPI use them to validate data.
WhenToUse: Any code that will be read by someone else, or any API boundary.

ShortDef: A decorator that writes the boilerplate (init, repr, equality) for classes that mostly hold data.
Details: `@dataclass class Point: x: int; y: int` is a complete class. Options give immutability (`frozen=True`) and ordering.
WhenToUse: Simple data containers where Pydantic's validation is not needed.

ShortDef: A lock in CPython that lets only one thread run Python code at a time.
Details: Threads still help for waiting on I/O, but CPU-bound work needs multiple processes. Recent Python versions offer an experimental free-threaded build that removes the lock.
WhenToUse: Choosing between threads, processes and asyncio.

ShortDef: Python's built-in way to run many I/O-bound tasks concurrently on one thread.
Details: `async def` functions are coroutines; `await` yields control while waiting. Great for many network calls; blocking calls inside a coroutine stall everything.
WhenToUse: Web servers, scrapers and clients making lots of concurrent requests.

ShortDef: A function that produces values one at a time, pausing between them, instead of building a whole list.
Details: `yield` returns a value and remembers where it stopped. Generators process huge or endless data with constant memory.
WhenToUse: Reading big files, streaming results or pipelines of transformations.

ShortDef: An object that sets something up and always cleans up afterwards, used with `with`.
Details: Files, locks, database connections and transactions use it so cleanup happens even when errors occur. Write your own with `contextlib.contextmanager`.
WhenToUse: Any resource that must be released.

ShortDef: A function that wraps another function to add behaviour, applied with the @ syntax.
Details: Used for routing in web frameworks, caching (`functools.cache`), timing, permissions and retries.
WhenToUse: Adding the same behaviour to many functions without repeating it.

ShortDef: Define a data shape with type hints and get automatic validation and conversion.
Details: Invalid input raises a clear error listing every problem. Version 2 is written in Rust and much faster. It powers FastAPI's request and response handling.
WhenToUse: Validating API input, configuration files and anything that crosses a trust boundary.

ShortDef: A modern web framework for building APIs with type hints, automatic validation and generated docs.
Details: Define endpoints as functions with typed parameters; FastAPI validates input, serialises output and serves interactive OpenAPI documentation. Supports async.

ShortDef: A batteries-included web framework: ORM, admin, authentication, forms and templates.
Details: Models define tables; migrations evolve them; the admin gives you a data editor for free. Opinionated structure helps large teams stay consistent.
WhenToUse: Content-heavy sites and apps that need a database and admin quickly.

ShortDef: The most popular Python testing framework: plain functions, simple asserts and powerful fixtures.
Details: Tests are functions named `test_*`; `assert` is enough. Fixtures provide setup, and parametrization runs one test across many inputs.

ShortDef: An extremely fast linter and formatter that replaces flake8, isort, Black and more.
Details: Configured in pyproject.toml; run `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format`. Catches bugs, unused imports and style issues in milliseconds.
WhenToUse: Every project, locally and in CI.
